name: Blockchain Scaling Solutions
description: Techniques for increasing blockchain throughput and reducing transaction costs without sacrificing security or decentralization — addressing the blockchain trilemma at the infrastructure level. Covers Layer 2 scaling approaches (state channels, Optimistic Rollups with fraud proofs, ZK Rollups with zero-knowledge proofs), sidechain and hybrid approaches (Validium, Plasma), Ethereum 2.0's sharding and beacon chain, and on-chain scaling improvements.

subskills.name: State & Payment Channels
subskills.description: Off-chain bilateral channels where two parties exchange signed state updates without submitting each to the blockchain. Payment channels: only the opening and closing transactions go on-chain; intermediate payments are instant and free (Lightning Network for Bitcoin, Raiden Network for Ethereum). State channels: generalized to arbitrary state (Connext, Counterfactual). Channel factories (virtual channels). Limitations: both parties must be online, capital locked in channels, routing complexity for multi-hop payments. Use cases: micropayments, gaming, high-frequency trading between known parties.

subskills.name: Optimistic Rollups & Fraud Proofs
subskills.description: Layer 2 scaling where transactions are processed off-chain by a Sequencer, batched, and posted to Ethereum calldata assuming validity (optimistically). Fraud proofs allow anyone to challenge invalid state transitions during a challenge period (7 days for Arbitrum One, Optimism). If a fraud proof succeeds, the malicious Sequencer is slashed. EVM-equivalent (Arbitrum Nitro) vs EVM-compatible (Optimism Bedrock). OP Stack (modular rollup framework used by Base, Optimism, Zora, Mantle). Arbitrum Stylus for multi-language execution. Fast withdrawal via liquidity bridges bypassing the 7-day window.

subskills.name: ZK Rollups & Zero-Knowledge Proofs
subskills.description: Layer 2 scaling using cryptographic validity proofs (zero-knowledge proofs) to prove that a batch of off-chain transactions is correct without revealing the underlying data. Unlike Optimistic Rollups, ZK Rollups have cryptographic finality — no challenge period required, enabling near-instant withdrawals. zkEVM variants: Type 1 (Ethereum-equivalent — Polygon Zero), Type 2 (EVM-equivalent — Scroll, Taiko), Type 3 (EVM-compatible — Polygon zkEVM), Type 4 (language-compatible — zkSync Era, StarkWare/StarkNet). ZK proof systems: zkSNARKs (Groth16, PLONK — succinct, no recursion limit) vs zkSTARKs (post-quantum, no trusted setup, larger proofs). ZK on Solana: Light Protocol.

subskills.name: Validium, Plasma & Sidechains
subskills.description: Hybrid and alternative approaches. Validium: like ZK Rollup but data availability is off-chain (a trusted committee or a decentralized availability layer like EigenDA/Celestia), enabling higher throughput at the cost of weaker data availability guarantees. StarkEx (dYdX v3, Sorare, Immutable X) uses Validium mode. Plasma: early L2 design (Plasma MVP, Plasma Cash) where fraud proofs protect child chains; limited by mass exit problem and poor support for arbitrary smart contracts. Polygon PoS sidechain: independent blockchain with its own validator set that bridges to Ethereum — not a true L2 (validators can collude). Gnosis Chain: xDAI sidechain for low-cost stable transactions.

subskills.name: Ethereum 2.0 — PoS, Beacon Chain & Danksharding
subskills.description: Ethereum's multi-phase upgrade from PoW to PoS and beyond. The Merge (2022): execution layer (EVM, transactions) merges with consensus layer (Beacon Chain, PoS validators). Post-Merge architecture: execution client (Geth/Nethermind/Besu) + consensus client (Prysm/Lighthouse/Lodestar) pairs. Proof of Stake: 32 ETH validator deposit, attestations, proposer/attestor roles, slashing conditions (double-signing), inactivity leak. EIP-4844 Proto-Danksharding (Cancun upgrade): blob transactions for L2 calldata — reduces L2 fees by 10-100x. Full Danksharding: 2D data availability sampling. Proposer-Builder Separation (PBS). The Surge, Scourge, Verge, Purge, Splurge roadmap phases.

subskills.name: On-Chain Scaling
subskills.description: Improvements to the base layer (L1) itself to increase throughput without moving computation off-chain. Covers: block gas limit increases (trade-off: higher hardware requirements for nodes), EIP-1559 base fee burn + tip mechanism (more predictable gas pricing, reduced ETH supply), calldata compression (EIP-4488, superseded by EIP-4844), EVMMAX (modular arithmetic instructions), EIP-3074 AUTH/AUTHCALL (account abstraction-light), EOF (EVM Object Format — container format for better bytecode analysis), verkle trees (replacing Merkle Patricia Tries for stateless clients). Solana's parallel transaction execution (Sealevel) as an alternative on-chain approach.

junior.description: Understands how Optimistic Rollups (Arbitrum, Optimism) work — Sequencer, fraud proofs, and challenge periods; can deploy contracts on L2s; understands state channel concepts.

mid.description: Understands ZK Rollup vs Optimistic Rollup trade-offs (finality, data availability, trust model), knows Validium and Plasma architectures, and can articulate Ethereum 2.0's PoS and EIP-4844 impact on L2 costs.

senior.description: Evaluates protocol-level scaling trade-offs (L1 vs L2 vs L3), contributes to or advises on rollup architecture decisions, understands ZK proof circuit development, and tracks Ethereum's scaling roadmap (Danksharding, Verge, Purge).
